title: How Many Crows in Agra
summary: Akbar asks how many crows in the city; Birbal gives an exact number and says if more, relatives visited, if fewer, they went visiting.
moral: A witty answer is better than an exact one

title: Birbal's Khichdi
summary: A poor man stands near a fire all night; Birbal proves it gave no warmth by 'cooking' khichdi from a rooftop fire.
moral: Justice requires understanding, not just rules

acts.name: challenge
acts.summary: Poor man must stand in cold all night

acts.name: denial
acts.summary: Akbar says distant fire helped the man

acts.name: lesson
acts.summary: Birbal cooks from rooftop to prove absurdity

title: The Well Dispute
summary: Two neighbors dispute a well; Birbal says the well owner must pay rent for storing water in the buyer's well.
moral: Clever logic exposes unfair claims

acts.name: dispute
acts.summary: Man sells well but not water

title: The Blind Men and the Elephant
summary: Birbal uses blind men touching an elephant to teach Akbar that truth depends on perspective.
moral: Truth has many facets; no single perspective captures it all

acts.name: demonstration
acts.summary: Blind men each describe elephant differently

title: Whose Beard Is It?
summary: A man steals another's beard-hair; Birbal makes the thief's own beard itch to confess.
moral: The guilty always betray themselves

acts.name: crime
acts.summary: Someone steals beard hair for a charm

acts.name: test
acts.summary: Birbal claims the sticks will grow

title: The Lines That Speak
summary: Akbar draws a line and asks Birbal to make it shorter without erasing; Birbal draws a longer line next to it.
moral: To diminish something, simply create something greater beside it

acts.name: solution
acts.summary: Draws longer line next to it

title: The Farmer and the Painting
summary: A farmer claims Birbal's painting is upside down; Birbal shows the farmer was looking at it wrong.
moral: Perspective changes everything

title: One Thousand Gold Coins
summary: Akbar gives Birbal 1000 gold coins to give away; Birbal gives them to the poorest, proving charity must be targeted.
moral: Charity is most effective when given to those who need it most

title: The Crows and the Owls
summary: Birbal advises Akbar on diplomacy by telling the fable of crows defeating owls through a spy.
moral: Intelligence gathering is more powerful than military strength

acts.name: fable
acts.summary: Birbal tells story of crows and owls

title: The Most Beautiful Child
summary: Akbar and Birbal see an ugly baby; its mother thinks it's the most beautiful. Birbal says every mother feels that way.
moral: Love sees beauty where others cannot

acts.name: walk
acts.summary: Akbar and Birbal walk through village

acts.name: observation
acts.summary: They see a mother adoring an ugly baby

title: Which Direction Does the Sunrise Come From?
summary: Birbal answers that wherever the emperor faces is east because the emperor is the sun.
moral: Wit and flattery combined make the perfect answer

acts.name: question
acts.summary: Akbar asks which way is east

title: The Ring in the River
summary: Akbar drops his ring in the river and Birbal finds it by pouring oil to calm the water.
moral: Simple science solves what seems impossible

title: Birbal's Sweet Reply
summary: Akbar asks if Birbal has ever been beaten; Birbal says yes, by Akbar's son at chess, and Akbar should be proud.
moral: A wise answer turns criticism into praise

acts.name: admission
acts.summary: Birbal admits losing to the prince

acts.name: pride
acts.summary: Akbar beams with pride for his son

title: The Oil Trader's Donkey
summary: A donkey falls in a river and its salt load dissolves, so it keeps falling on purpose; the owner loads it with cotton instead.
moral: Every trick works only once

acts.name: accident
acts.summary: Donkey falls in river, salt dissolves

acts.name: lesson
acts.summary: Owner loads cotton which gets heavier

title: The Foolish Thief
summary: Birbal catches a thief by making all suspects hold magic sticks — the thief trims his, thinking it will grow.
moral: The guilty conscience reveals itself

acts.name: test
acts.summary: Birbal gives magic sticks to all suspects

acts.name: catch
acts.summary: Only the thief's stick is shorter

title: Three Questions of the Emperor
summary: Akbar asks: What is the greatest thing? Where is heaven? Who lies the most? Birbal answers using everyday examples.
moral: The deepest truths hide in simple observations

title: The Washerman and the Pot
summary: A washerman's pot is stuck on his donkey's head; Birbal solves it by putting grain inside for the donkey to eat downward.
moral: Work with nature, not against it

acts.name: solution
acts.summary: Grain lures donkey to tilt head down

title: The Singing Lesson
summary: Akbar sings badly; everyone praises him except Birbal who says he sings 'even better than the court singer' — sarcastic honesty.
moral: True friends tell the truth, even uncomfortable ones

title: A Small Wish
summary: Akbar offers any wish; Birbal asks to be allowed to always speak the truth, the most powerful wish of all.
moral: The freedom to speak truth is the greatest privilege

acts.name: wish
acts.summary: Asks for freedom to always speak truth

title: The Mango Tree Dispute
summary: Two women claim a mango tree; Birbal says cut it down — the real owner protests, revealing herself.
moral: True ownership shows in the willingness to sacrifice for what you love

acts.name: truth
acts.summary: Real owner begs to spare it
